papers_read.title_as_printed: Predicting cognitive decline: Deep-learning reveals subtle brain changes in pre-MCI stage (Yue, Pan, Li et al., J Prev Alz Dis 2025)
Early progression detection from MCI to AD using multi-view MRI for enhanced assisted living (Rahim et al., Image and Vision Computing 2025)

what_each_reports.P-146: ROI-based CNN trained on ADNI-1 (AD+pMCI vs NC+sMCI) yields a Progressive Index applied to cognitively normal/SCD people: ADNI-2 NC/SCD-to-MCI within ~3 years AUC 0.7048; CLAS (109 NC/SCD, 7-year follow-up) PI alone AUC 0.711; PI combined with age, gender, education and an associative-learning score in logistic regression AUC 0.812 (95% CI 0.725-0.900).
what_each_reports.P-41: Multi-plane 2D CNN heterogeneous ensemble with CBAM and multi-head attention, ADNI (192 subjects: 96 sMCI vs 81 pMCI + 15 AD in the positive class), subject-level split 71/10/15 per class; test accuracy 91.77%, sensitivity 87.69%, specificity 88.53%, AUC 92.87%.

quantity_a: AUC for predicting conversion from normal cognition or SCD to (amnestic) MCI over 7 years in the CLAS community cohort, from an MRI-derived index plus demographic and neuropsychological variables.
quantity_b: AUC for separating stable MCI from progressive MCI (MCI-to-AD within M18-M48) pooled with established AD, from baseline structural MRI slices only, on a 30-subject ADNI test set.
incompatible_if_same: Not meaningful: 0.812 (0.725-0.900) vs 0.929 (+/- 3.58) are for different transitions; neither paper claims the ordering the other refutes.

gates.task: mismatch in substance: both coded T2, but P-146 predicts NC/SCD-to-MCI conversion while P-41 predicts MCI-to-AD (with AD cases in the positive class).
gates.dataset_family: mismatch for the cited figure: P-146's 0.812 comes from CLAS (Shanghai), P-41 is ADNI only. P-146's ADNI-2 result (0.7048) is still NC/SCD-to-MCI, not MCI-to-AD.
gates.validation_tier: mismatch: P-146's CLAS result is an external application of an ADNI-1-trained network (with the clinical logistic model fitted in CLAS); P-41 is an internal ADNI hold-out.
gates.modality_family: partial: both structural MRI, but P-146's 0.812 adds demographics and a neuropsychological score, whereas P-41 is MRI only.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: both ROC-AUC, but for different endpoints (future MCI in cognitively normal people over 7 years vs future AD in MCI patients, with prevalent AD added) and different populations.
performance_validity: flag not tripped (0.929 < 0.97). P-41's test set is 30 subjects and its positive class includes 15 established-AD patients, which inflates discrimination relative to a pure sMCI/pMCI contrast.
independence: Distinct studies and authors; both use ADNI data (P-146 for training/ADNI-2 validation, P-41 for everything), so participant overlap is possible for the ADNI components but not for P-146's CLAS figure.
grounds: P-146's AUC 0.812 is for conversion from normal cognition/SCD to MCI over seven years in CLAS, whereas P-41's AUC 0.929 is for stable vs progressive MCI plus AD in ADNI, so the transition predicted differs.
P-41's positive class mixes progressive MCI with 15 established AD patients, so its population differs from any conversion-only cohort.
The cited P-146 figure also adds demographic and neuropsychological predictors to MRI and comes from a different dataset family (CLAS vs ADNI), with no waiver on record.

evidence_quotes.quote: Better performance for prediction progression to MCI in CLAS was obtained when the PI score was combined with clinical measures (AUC = 0.812; 95 %CI: 0.725-0.900).

the PI value combined with a neuropsychological scale score (associative learning) and General demographic information (age, gender and years of education) can effectively predict the conversion of MCI in the CLAS cohort after 7 years, with an AUC of 0.812
we added 15 patients with AD to the pMCI group to help the model learn both the progressive and fully diseased brain patterns simultaneously.

The MHA classifier in the same heterogeneous ensemble outperformed the LSTM with an accuracy of 91.77% +/-3.14, sensitivity of 87.69% +/-3.24, specificity of 88.53% +/-3.53, and an impressive AUC of 92.87% +/-3.58.

record_defects: dataset_family_equivalence true is wrong for the cited figure: P-146's AUC 0.812 is from CLAS, not ADNI.
task_equivalence true is wrong in substance: P-146 predicts NC/SCD-to-MCI, P-41 predicts sMCI vs pMCI+AD; the shared 'T2' code hides this.
claim_a still cites P-310 (repointed to P-146); claim_a omits that 0.812 is an MRI-plus-clinical logistic model, not the MRI network alone (PI alone: 0.711 CLAS, 0.7048 ADNI-2).
Index registry row for P-146 gives Best_Metric 'not reported' and a truncated abstract fragment as Method_Architecture; the paper reports AUCs 0.7048, 0.711 and 0.812.
resolution_status 'partially_resolved_candidate' rests on a generic list of ~57 'bridging' papers with no separating condition.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Only an MCI-to-AD result from P-146 (it reports none; its ADNI-1 training labels are AD+pMCI vs NC+sMCI but no held-out AUC for that contrast is given) would share P-41's estimand.
